target_customer: Streetwear and sneaker fans who buy and sell limited releases; later collectors of sneakers, NFTs and cards via membership
problem: Fans of limited streetwear drops had no peer to peer marketplace for the full range of items beyond sneakers; Bump let sellers list items with PayPal buyer protection.
business_model: Marketplace take rate (6 percent seller fee plus PayPal 2.9 percent); later subscription membership (Secured)

founders.name: Jack Ryder
founders.background_notes: YC page: now building Flare, an AI accounting firm. TechCrunch 2019 says he and Howarth traded streetwear and sneakers before starting the company.

founders.name: Sam Howarth
founders.background_notes: No background listed on YC page.

competitors.name: GOAT
competitors.traction_then: Supported only sneakers at the time per TechCrunch

technical_complexity.rationale: An iOS marketplace app with messaging and PayPal payments, plus fraud controls with device ID blocking; standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Liquidity among streetwear users helped, but sellers could list elsewhere and incumbents authenticated items, which Bump did not.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: StockX traffic more than doubled in 2018 per Glossy while others stayed flat; no source on a Bump acquisition.

market_need_then: At launch Bump reported over 200,000 users and 5.5 million messages (TechCrunch, February 2018), and nearly 2 million registered users by April 2019.

rebrands.why: YC page now names the company Secured with a sneaker, NFT and web3 membership focus; no source states a date or reason.

branding.community_and_virality: App reported 5.5 million messages among 200,000 users by February 2018, showing active community use.

brand_strength.rationale: Reasonable early traction but the name is common (many unrelated Bump companies) and no brand press was found.

pivots.to: Membership tools for sneaker, NFT and web3 investors (Secured)

outcome_analysis: Bump grew quickly to about 2 million registered users and raised a 7.5 million dollar Series A in April 2019 led by e.ventures, then moved to a subscription for collectors under the name Secured, now listed inactive. No post-mortem was found; competition from authenticated marketplaces such as StockX and GOAT is a plausible but unconfirmed factor.
notes: YC lists no website; no company site was fetched. TechCrunch (April 2019) says the round also involved a move from New York to London; the stated total raised was not given, so earlier rounds may be missing. The Series A is stated by TechCrunch and a second outlet (nationaldailyng) with e.ventures leading. Search for a shutdown cause found only unrelated NFT news, so the cause is not public. GOAT and StockX funding and traction are not given in the cited article.
